subject: history
title: Origins of the Cold War 1945-49
welcome_lead: From the Grand Alliance to the division of Europe.
meta_desc: A-Level Cold War adventure on Yalta, Potsdam, Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan and the founding of NATO 1949.
final_note: You can analyse rival explanations for the breakdown of wartime cooperation.

concepts.def: 4-11 February 1945 meeting of Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill agreeing UN creation, German occupation zones and 'free elections' in Eastern Europe.
17 July-2 August 1945 meeting of Stalin, Truman and Churchill/Attlee; revealed widening Allied disagreement over Eastern Europe and reparations.
George Kennan's 1946 cable and 1947 'Sources of Soviet Conduct' article advocating containment of Soviet expansion.
12 March 1947 address pledging US support to peoples 'resisting attempted subjugation', triggered by Greek and Turkish crises.
European Recovery Programme (June 1947 proposal, 1948 act) providing ~$13 billion in aid to Western Europe.
North Atlantic Treaty Organisation founded on 4 April 1949 by 12 states; Article 5 mutual defence pledge.

walkthroughs.body_html: Yalta agreed Germany's division into four zones and 'free elections' in liberated Europe. By Potsdam, Roosevelt was dead, Churchill replaced by Attlee and Truman knew of the atomic bomb. Disputes over reparations and the Polish government were unresolved. Soviet-imposed regimes consolidated across Eastern Europe; Churchill's Fulton 'Iron Curtain' speech (5 March 1946) named the divide.

Kennan's Long Telegram (February 1946) framed Soviet expansionism as ideologically driven. Britain's February 1947 withdrawal from Greece prompted the Truman Doctrine. Secretary of State Marshall's Harvard speech (5 June 1947) launched the Marshall Plan; Stalin rejected it for the Eastern bloc and created Cominform (September 1947).

The Czechoslovak coup (February 1948) alarmed the West. Currency reform in the Western zones triggered the Berlin Blockade (24 June 1948-12 May 1949), met by the Berlin Airlift of over 2.3 million tonnes of supplies. NATO followed on 4 April 1949. In May 1949 the Federal Republic was founded, in October the German Democratic Republic. The Soviet atomic test (August 1949) ended the US nuclear monopoly.

mcqs.q: Why did Stalin reject the Marshall Plan?
options: He saw it as dollar imperialism that would pull Eastern Europe into the US orbit; he set up Comecon as an Eastern bloc alternative and blocked satellite states from joining.
Stalin rejected the Marshall Plan because the USSR did not need money after WWII.
Stalin rejected the Marshall Plan because it required countries to fight Germany again.
Stalin blockaded Berlin to stop Nazis escaping to the West.

mcqs.q: Why did Stalin blockade West Berlin in 1948?
options: Stalin blockaded Berlin because he wanted to invade Western Europe.
Stalin rejected the Marshall Plan because it required countries to fight Germany again.
To force the Western Allies out of Berlin in response to the merging of their zones, introduction of the Deutschmark, and creation of a separate West German state.
Stalin blockaded Berlin to stop Nazis escaping to the West.
